subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: Should `textTransforms.output` keep rewriting every structured tool-call argument string, or should OpenClaw add a path/tool-boundary rule that exempts filesystem-looking values from rebrand-style replacements?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally restore transformed tool-call arguments for masking plugins, but this issue shows the same contract can silently misroute filesystem operations when replacements match path segments.

options.title: Adopt a path-aware boundary
options.body: Preserve ordinary text and masking transforms while exempting filesystem-looking tool argument values, then require tests and live dual-directory proof before merge.

options.title: Keep current transform semantics
options.body: Document that plugin authors must avoid path-sensitive replacements or use `before_tool_call` for custom decoding, accepting the reported misrouting risk for rebrand-like transforms.

options.title: Redesign as typed policy
options.body: Pause the linked fork PR and design a typed tool-argument transform policy so path, secret, and display transforms are no longer one global string replacement chain.

recommendation.title: Adopt a path-aware boundary
recommendation.body: Preserve ordinary text and masking transforms while exempting filesystem-looking tool argument values, then require tests and live dual-directory proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the text-transform surface and merged the current structured tool-call argument transform behavior.
